source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: Quadratic variation up to a common stop. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source.original_text:
Evaluate the original finite Itô row at a common bounded stopping time capped by the evaluation time. The dyadic squared-increment sum of this stopped row converges in L¹ to the original square energy accumulated up to that stop, with integrable signed error at every level.

One Euclidean Brownian motion under the sample measure μ, relative to the given filtration. The coordinates in a finite index set J come from this same motion.
The sample measure is finite. The horizon T is positive and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions.
Each coordinate input is progressive and product-space square integrable. One [0,T]-valued stopping time τ is shared by all coordinates and satisfies 0 ≤ τ(ω) ≤ T at every sample point.

\begin{gathered}R^\tau_t=\sum_j\int_0^{t\wedge\tau}\eta_j(s)\,dB_s^j,\qquad E^\tau=\sum_j\int_{[0,\tau]}\eta_j(t)^2\,dt,\\ \int\left|\sum_i(\Delta_i R^\tau)^2-E^\tau\right|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0.\end{gathered}

lean.statement:
theorem anonymous_target.{u_1,
    u_2}
  {Omega : Type u_1} {J : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Omega] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
  {filtration : MeasureTheory.Filtration NNReal inferInstance} {mu : MeasureTheory.Measure Omega}
  [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure mu] {T : NNReal} {B : NNReal → Omega → EuclideanSpace ℝ J}
  (hB :
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.BrownianMotion.IsStandardBrownianMotionWithFiltration B
      filtration mu)
  (hT : 0 < T)
  (hUsual : AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration mu)
  (eta :
    J → AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2.ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu T)
  (tau : Omega → NNReal)
  (htau :
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.StoppingTime.IsChewiStoppingTime filtration fun omega =>
      ↑(tau omega))
  (htauT : ∀ (omega : Omega), tau omega ≤ T) :
  have hcoord := ⋯;
  have row := fun t omega =>
    ∑ j,
      AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoIntegralProcess.itoIntegralProcess (eta j) hT ⋯ hUsual
        (Min.min (tau omega) t) omega;
  have error := fun level omega =>
    have times :=
      AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.SampledElementaryApproximation.regularGridTimes
        (AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.SampledElementaryApproximation.dyadicMesh T level)
        (2 ^ level);
    ∑ i, (row (times i.succ) omega - row (times i.castSucc) omega) ^ 2 -
      ∑ j,
        ∫ (t : NNReal) in Set.Iic (tau omega),
          (eta j).process t omega ^ 2 ∂AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.TimeMeasure.upTo T;
  (∀ (level : ℕ), MeasureTheory.Integrable (error level) mu) ∧
    Filter.Tendsto (fun level => ∫ (omega : Omega), |error level omega| ∂mu) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)

blind_reconstruction.text:
Objects: Write R_+=[0,infinity), and let lambda_T be Lebesgue measure on [0,T], transported to R_+ (the given comap of volume restricted to [0,T]). All time integrals below use this measure unless indicated otherwise. For n in N put t[n,i]=i*T/2^n for i=0,...,2^n, and Delta_i^n Z=Z(t[n,i+1])-Z(t[n,i]). A ProgressiveL2Integrand eta on horizon T is a real process eta(t,omega), strongly progressive for the filtration, with (omega,t) -> eta(t,omega) in L^2(mu x lambda_T). I_T^j(eta) denotes the supplied completed continuous Ito process driven by the scalar coordinate B_j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j: the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic-integral approximations off their null uniform-Cauchy bad set, zero on that bad set, and held constant after T; at each t<=T it agrees almost everywhere with the L^2-completion integral up to t. Define R(t,omega)=sum_j I_T^j(eta_j)(min(tau(omega),t),omega). Define e_n(omega)=sum_i (Delta_i^n R(omega))^2-sum_j integral_{s<=tau(omega)} eta_j(s,omega)^2 d lambda_T(s). The integrand's toLp operation is its L^2 equivalence class represented by (omega,t)->eta(t,omega).

Domains: Omega measurable; J finite with decidable equality; mu finite; filtration on R_+; T>0; vector Brownian B in R^J; eta:J->ProgressiveL2Integrand(filtration,mu,T); tau:Omega->R_+.

Quantifiers: Universally spaces,filtration,mu,T,B; Brownian,positive-T,usual assumptions; eta,tau; stopping-time and bound assumptions. Conclusion first forall n, then the limit as n->infinity.

Assumptions: The vector Brownian hypothesis means B(0,omega)=0 for every omega; increments on finite families of pairwise disjoint half-open intervals are jointly independent; every continuous real linear functional ell sends B(t)-B(s), s<t, to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||^2; paths are mu-almost surely continuous. B is strongly adapted, and for every s<=t the increment B(t)-B(s) is independent of the sigma-algebra filtration(s). The filtration is right continuous, and every mu-null subset of Omega belongs to filtration(t) for every t>=0 (completeness at each time). The coercion omega->tau(omega) into extended nonnegative reals is a stopping time for the filtration (the supplied IsChewiStoppingTime is exactly IsStoppingTime); tau(omega)<=T for every omega.

Conclusion: Every e_n is mu-integrable, and integral_Omega |e_n(omega)|dmu tends to zero as n->infinity.

Scopes: This is L^1 convergence of the stopped quadratic-variation error to zero. The stopping-time bound is pointwise, not only almost sure. Integrals restrict to s<=tau(omega); the partition remains the deterministic dyadic partition of [0,T].

Constant dependencies: No bound or rate constant is stated. e_n depends on T,tau,eta and the completed Ito processes; convergence may depend on all input data.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoContinuousRowQV
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.RandomStoppingProcessConsistency

/-! # Dyadic quadratic variation at one common bounded stopping time -/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoStoppedRowQV

open Filter MeasureTheory Set
open scoped NNReal BigOperators
open BrownianMotion ProgressiveL2 StoppingTime EuclideanBrownianCoordinates
  ItoIntegralProcess SampledElementaryApproximation DyadicElementaryRefinement
  ProgressiveL2Stopping RandomStoppingProcessConsistency ItoContinuousRowQV

/-- Evaluate the actual Itô row at the common stopped time. Its dyadic
quadratic variation converges in `L¹` to the original energy up to the stop. -/
theorem tendsto_dyadic_stopped_ito_row_quadraticVariation_L1
    {Omega J : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Omega] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
    {filtration : Filtration ℝ≥0 (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Omega)}
    {mu : Measure Omega} [IsFiniteMeasure mu] {T : ℝ≥0}
    {B : ℝ≥0 → Omega → EuclideanSpace ℝ J}
    (hB : IsStandardBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration mu) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hUsual : SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration mu)
    (eta : J → ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu T)
    (tau : Omega → ℝ≥0)
    (htau : IsChewiStoppingTime filtration (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)))
    (htauT : ∀ omega, tau omega ≤ T) :
    let hcoord := (coordinateFamily hB).isBrownian
    let row := fun t omega =>
      ∑ j : J, itoIntegralProcess (eta j) hT (hcoord j) hUsual (min (tau omega) t) omega
    let error := fun level omega =>
      let times := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T level) (2 ^ level)
      (∑ i : Fin (2 ^ level), (row (times i.succ) omega -
        row (times i.castSucc) omega)^2) -
      ∑ j : J, ∫ t in Set.Iic (tau omega), (eta j).process t omega ^ 2 ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)
    (∀ level, Integrable (error level) mu) ∧
      Tendsto (fun level => ∫ omega, |error level omega| ∂mu) atTop (nhds 0) := by
  intro hcoord row error
  let times (level : ℕ) := regularGridTimes (dyadicMesh T level) (2 ^ level)
  let stoppedEta (j : J) := stop (eta j) (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)) htau
  let stoppedRow (t : ℝ≥0) (omega : Omega) :=
    ∑ j : J, itoIntegralProcess (stoppedEta j) hT (hcoord j) hUsual t omega
  let stoppedError (level : ℕ) (omega : Omega) :=
    (∑ i : Fin (2 ^ level), (stoppedRow (times level i.succ) omega -
      stoppedRow (times level i.castSucc) omega)^2) -
    ∑ j : J, ∫ t, (stoppedEta j).process t omega ^ 2 ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)
  have htime (level : ℕ) (k : Fin (2 ^ level + 1)) : times level k ≤ T :=
    ((regularGridTimes_strictMono (dyadicMesh_pos hT level) _).monotone
      (Fin.le_last k)).trans_eq (regularDyadic_last_time T level)
  have hAt (level : ℕ) (k : Fin (2 ^ level + 1)) (j : J) :
      ∀ᵐ omega ∂mu,
        itoIntegralProcess (stoppedEta j) hT (hcoord j) hUsual (times level k) omega =
          itoIntegralProcess (eta j) hT (hcoord j) hUsual (min (tau omega) (times level k)) omega :=
    itoIntegralProcess_stop_ae (eta j) hT tau htau htauT (hcoord j) hUsual (htime level k)
  have hEnergy (j : J) (omega : Omega) :
      (∫ t, (stoppedEta j).process t omega ^ 2 ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)) =
        ∫ t in Set.Iic (tau omega), (eta j).process t omega ^ 2 ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T) := by
    rw [← integral_indicator measurableSet_Iic]
    apply integral_congr_ae
    filter_upwards [] with t
    change (if (t : WithTop ℝ≥0) ≤ (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)
      then (eta j).process t omega else 0)^2 = _
    by_cases ht : t ≤ tau omega
    · rw [if_pos (WithTop.coe_le_coe.mpr ht),
        Set.indicator_of_mem (show t ∈ Set.Iic (tau omega) from ht)]
    · rw [if_neg (fun h => ht (WithTop.coe_le_coe.mp h)),
        Set.indicator_of_notMem (show t ∉ Set.Iic (tau omega) from ht)]
      norm_num
  have hEq (level : ℕ) : stoppedError level =ᵐ[mu] error level := by
    filter_upwards [ae_all_iff.2 fun k => ae_all_iff.2 (hAt level k)] with omega homega
    have hRow (k : Fin (2 ^ level + 1)) : stoppedRow (times level k) omega =
        row (times level k) omega :=
      Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j _ => homega k j)
    simp only [stoppedError, error, hEnergy, hRow]
    rfl
  have hLimit : (∀ level, Integrable (stoppedError level) mu) ∧
      Tendsto (fun level => ∫ omega, |stoppedError level omega| ∂mu) atTop (nhds 0) :=
    tendsto_dyadic_ito_row_quadraticVariation_L1 hB hT hUsual stoppedEta
  refine ⟨fun level => (hLimit.1 level).congr (hEq level), ?_⟩
  exact (tendsto_congr' (Eventually.of_forall fun level =>
    integral_congr_ae ((hEq level).mono fun _ h => congrArg abs h))).1 hLimit.2

#print axioms tendsto_dyadic_stopped_ito_row_quadraticVariation_L1

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ItoStoppedRowQV

steps.title: Identify the stopped row at every grid endpoint
steps.text: Use the fixed-time stopping theorem at all endpoints of one finite grid. This identifies the actual stopped row with the completed row of closed stopped integrands almost surely.
steps.lean:
have hAt (level : ℕ) (k : Fin (2 ^ level + 1)) (j : J) :
      ∀ᵐ omega ∂mu,

    itoIntegralProcess_stop_ae (eta j) hT tau htau htauT (hcoord j) hUsual (htime level k)

steps.title: Identify the stopped energy
steps.text: Squaring the stopped integrand preserves its indicator. Integrate the original coefficient squared on the closed interval ending at τ.
steps.lean:
have hEnergy (j : J) (omega : Omega) :
      (∫ t, (stoppedEta j).process t omega ^ 2 ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T)) =
        ∫ t in Set.Iic (tau omega), (eta j).process t omega ^ 2 ∂(TimeMeasure.upTo T) := by

steps.title: Apply the progressive-row theorem
steps.text: Stopping preserves progressive L². Replace the row values and energy at each level by their identified counterparts and use the already proved L¹ limit.

    filter_upwards [ae_all_iff.2 fun k => ae_all_iff.2 (hAt level k)] with omega homega
    have hRow (k : Fin (2 ^ level + 1)) : stoppedRow (times level k) omega =
